hypothesis: At +2, the paid boost dominates every contest: 100% of responders who can afford fee plus boost buy it (baseline holdout audit), and boosted contests win 77% versus 55% plain, so any responder holding 2 Prestige converts to an almost-certain cancellation. That auto-purchase drives the cancellation churn of 7.1 canceled claims per game (88% of claims canceled). At +1 the boost no longer overwhelms the 0-2 equipment differential: challenge success falls toward the plain rate, claims survive more often, and paying for the boost becomes a judgment call a player could reasonably decline.
prediction: Cancellations per finished game fall by at least 30% (from about 7.1 to at most 5.0) on both screen and holdout; boosted-contest win rate falls from 0.77 toward 0.65 or below; claims won by acclamation rise from 0.12 to at least 0.25; median rounds do not rise; contest_offered_rate and responder affordability stay at baseline levels (about 0.66 and 0.78); all four profiles still win.
refutation_evidence: Cancellations per game fall by less than 30%; or the first challenger's win share rises above one half (the game becomes a first-proclaim race); or acclamations explode past about 0.6 while displacement comebacks vanish; or any mechanical or counterplay gate fails on either suite.
